Quick engineering readout:

- Latency: For the shortlisted variants we can hit p95 targets with the right instance mix. Rough numbers (p95 generation only, 8 token warmup, single request):
  - Redwood-Adapter-13B-q4o @ 8k context: ~420–520ms p95 on A100-class nodes (we'd recommend dedicated capacity for predictable behavior).
  - Redwood-Adapter-13B-q4o @ 16k context: ~700–900ms p95; depends on batch size and KV cache warmness.
  - Open-Lite-7B @ 2–4k: ~160–260ms p95.
  - Redwood-Base-2.7B fallback: ~110–200ms p95.

- Token throughput: Baseline peak estimates (per-hour) assuming continuous business-hour load and 25% cache hit from prefix/document caching:
  - Hybrid route (40% Adapter-13B, 40% Open-Lite-7B, 20% Redwood-Base): ~2.6M tokens/hour peak.
  - If caching is lower (10%): ~3.1M tokens/hour.

- Runtime notes: For 16k windows we strongly recommend: quantization profile q4o, pinned GPU pools, and a small KV-cache layer per customer to avoid repeated context recomputation. Document-level caching is supported; we can store the embeddings + chunked prefetched KV entries for repeated follow-ups.

Action items for Monica & Sofia: I will prepare a short sizing worksheet for the Dedicated pool (instances, GPUs, expected concurrency) by Monday. Also flagged JIRA-ENG-1127 for the 16k stress test.

Ben
